class.name: BoneClothSimulator3D
class.brief_description: A [SkeletonModifier3D] that sways bone chains linked to their neighbours, so a skirt of several chains moves as one surface.
class.description: This [SkeletonModifier3D] sways skirts, capes, hair and tails, and returns them toward the animated pose as [SpringBoneSimulator3D] does. Its solver is ported from KawaiiPhysics: each joint keeps its speed, is pulled toward its pose, is pushed out of the collisions, then is held inside its angle limit and at its bone's length. If you set up [method set_root_bone_name] and [method set_end_bone_name], the bones from the root down to the end are one chain. The root follows the pose and the bones below it are simulated. A chain whose root bone is a joint of an earlier chain is a branch of it and follows that joint, so wings and forked hair can be built from several chains. List the trunk before its branches. With [member link_mode] set, each chain is linked to its neighbour in the list at every depth below the root. The links keep the joints at their rest distance and collide with the collisions as lines, so a leg cannot pass between two chains. The values apply to every chain of the node. Each is scaled along the chains by its damping curve, read at the joint's share of the length from the root: [code]0.0[/code] at the root, [code]1.0[/code] at the farthest tip of its tree. Use one node for each part that needs other values, such as one for the skirt and one for the hair. Each [BoneClothCollision3D] child of this node is a collision for every joint of the node, in the order of the scene tree. The simulation runs in fixed steps of 1/60 s, at most 4 a frame; time beyond that is dropped. [member drag/value], [member stiffness/value] and [member link_stiffness] are amounts per step. Between steps the joints are drawn where the last step's motion carries them, so the cloth moves every frame on a display faster than 60 Hz. [b]Note:[/b] Most methods in this class take an [code]index[/code] parameter. This parameter specifies which chain to use (e.g. [code]chains/<index>/root_bone_name[/code]).

method.name: apply_preset
method.description: Copies the values of [param preset] onto this node. The chains, [member link_mode] and the collisions are not in a preset and stay as they are. The curves are copied, so editing them afterwards leaves the preset's file as it was.

method.name: get_end_bone
method.description: Returns the end bone index of the chain.

method.name: get_end_bone_name
method.description: Returns the end bone name of the chain.

method.name: get_root_bone
method.description: Returns the root bone index of the chain.

method.name: get_root_bone_name
method.description: Returns the root bone name of the chain.

method.name: make_preset
method.description: Returns a new [BoneClothPreset] holding this node's values, with copies of its curves. Save it with [method ResourceSaver.save] to apply it to other nodes; [b]Save Preset...[/b] in the node's menu in the 3D editor's toolbar does the same.

method.name: reset
method.description: Puts every joint back on the current bone pose at the next modification, at rest. It is useful when the pose jumps, for example right after a call to [method AnimationPlayer.play] without a blend, where the cloth would otherwise swing hard toward the new pose.

method.name: set_end_bone
method.description: Sets the end bone index of the chain, and its name from the skeleton. [code]-1[/code] is no bone. An index past the skeleton's bones prints a warning and sets [code]-1[/code].

method.name: set_end_bone_name
method.description: Sets the end bone name of the chain, and its index from the skeleton. The end bone must be the root bone or a bone below it. The name is kept when the skeleton has no such bone; the chain then prints an error when it is built and is not simulated, while the other chains run.

method.name: set_root_bone
method.description: Sets the root bone index of the chain, and its name from the skeleton. [code]-1[/code] is no bone. An index past the skeleton's bones prints a warning and sets [code]-1[/code].

method.name: set_root_bone_name
method.description: Sets the root bone name of the chain, and its index from the skeleton. The root bone follows the pose and is not simulated. The name is kept when the skeleton has no such bone; the chain then prints an error when it is built and is not simulated, while the other chains run.

members.member: The number of chains.
The curve that scales [member drag/value] along the chains. Without a curve, or with a curve that has no points, the scale is [code]1.0[/code].
The share of each joint's speed lost in a step, from [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code]. The greater the value, the more suppressed the swaying.

The length of a virtual joint added after the end bone of every chain, in the end bone's direction from its parent. A bone turns toward the joint below it, so without this joint the end bone cannot turn. [code]0.0[/code] adds none.

The acceleration applied to every joint, in world space. [b]Note:[/b] Unlike [SpringBoneSimulator3D]'s gravity, which is a constant velocity, this is an acceleration, in m/s^2. [member stiffness/value] pulls the joints back toward the pose, so gravity bends the chains only part of the way.

The share of the skeleton's movement and turning the cloth feels, from [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code]. The rest carries the cloth along with the skeleton. Only a change in the motion moves the cloth against it: at a steady speed or turning rate, the cloth is carried along.

Softens sudden starts and stops. The cloth feels the skeleton move at a speed that eases toward its real speed, faster at lower values. [code]0.0[/code] turns it off. Taken from Magica Cloth 2's World Inertia Smoothing.

The highest speed of each joint, not counting the part the skeleton's motion carries. A capped speed swings better, hair in a turn above all, but a low cap weakens the push out of the collisions. [code]0.0[/code] turns it off. Taken from Magica Cloth 2's particle speed limit.
The curve that scales [member limit_angle/value] along the chains. Without a curve, or with a curve that has no points, the scale is [code]1.0[/code].

The widest angle each bone can lean away from its animated direction, in radians. The bone is held inside a cone around that direction. [code]0.0[/code] turns the limit off; with it on, a joint whose curve brings the angle to [code]0.0[/code] is held to its animated direction. Check [b]Show Limit Angle[/b] in the node's menu in the 3D editor's toolbar to draw the cones.
How the chains are linked to each other, in the order they are listed. A branch that starts below its trunk's root is not linked.

How strongly the links hold neighbouring joints at their rest distance, from [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code]. At [code]1.0[/code] each step restores the distance, as KawaiiPhysics' links do. At [code]0.0[/code] the distance is free, but the links still collide with the collisions as lines.
The skeleton's speed above which the cloth feels no more of its movement. A fast character then does not throw its cloth further.
The curve that scales [member radius/value] along the chains. Without a curve, or with a curve that has no points, the scale is [code]1.0[/code].
The joint radius, which the collisions keep out. A link takes the mean of its two joints' radii.
The skeleton's turning speed above which the cloth feels no more of its turning, in radians per second.
The curve that scales [member stiffness/value] along the chains. Without a curve, or with a curve that has no points, the scale is [code]1.0[/code].

The share of the way to its animated place each joint is pulled in a step, from [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code]. The greater the value, the faster it returns to the pose. At [code]0.0[/code] the chain does not return to the pose. [b]Note:[/b] This is KawaiiPhysics' stiffness. [SpringBoneSimulator3D]'s stiffness runs from [code]0.0[/code] to [code]4.0[/code] in another formula, so its values do not carry over.

A turn of the skeleton larger than this in one frame, in radians, is taken as a teleport: the cloth goes on as if the skeleton had kept its last motion. Taken from Magica Cloth 2's teleport in its Keep mode.
A move of the skeleton farther than this in one frame is taken as a teleport: the cloth goes on as if the skeleton had kept its last motion. Taken from Magica Cloth 2's teleport in its Keep mode.

constants.constant: Each chain is linked to the next one in the list, as for a cape or a skirt open at the front.
Each chain is linked to the next one in the list and the last to the first, as for a skirt all around. With two chains it is the same as [constant LINK_MODE_SEQUENTIAL].
